title: WPMS/3221/2019 of MOHIT KUMAR Vs DISTRICT MAGISTRATE HARIDWAR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 3221 of 2019
Mohit Kumar .......Petitioner
Versus
District Magistrate Haridwar & others .......Respondents
Mr. Anil Kumar Dabral, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. J.C. Pande, Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Ashutosh Thakral, Advocate for the respondent no.2.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Dated: 27th November, 2019
RAMESH RANGANATHAN, C.J. (Oral)
 This Writ Petition is filed questioning the oral direction
allegedly issued by the District Magistrate, Haridwar prohibiting the sale of
chicken within the territorial limits of Haridwar district.
2. The petitioner, who is running a chicken centre in Laksar,
claims that such direction of the District Magistrate, Haridwar is
unauthorized and is contrary to law.
3. In the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of the Food Safety
Officer, Laksar, Haridwar district, it is stated that the petitioner does not
have a valid registration certificate regarding the Food Safety & Standard
Act, 2006; as per Rule 2.5.1 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing
and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, 'chicken' also falls
within its ambit; the District Magistrate, Haridwar had only sought to
implement the orders passed by the High Court from time to time and,
therefore, no interference is called for.
4. A Division Bench of this Court had, by its order in Writ
Petition (PIL) No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018, directed all illegal
Slaughter Houses in the State of Uttarakhand to be sealed; and all the
Executive Officers of the Local Self Government, Municipal Corporation,
Municipalities, Nagar Panchayats and other Panchayats to ensure that no
animal was slaughtered in the public streets/paths/roads and in open spaces.
The State Government was also directed to ensure that no Slaughter House
was permitted to run without complying with the Food Safety and Standards
(Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011.

2
5. While Mr. Anil K. Dabral, learned counsel for the petitioner,
would contend that the petitioner has a valid registration certificate, the
order of the Division Bench in Writ Petition (PIL) No.152 of 2018 dated
20.09.2018 prohibits operation of illegal Slaughter Houses and the slaughter
of animals. The action being taken by the District Magistrate, Haridwar, to
prohibit sale of chicken does appear to be in compliance with the order of
the Division Bench in Writ Petition (PIL) No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018.
6. Mr. Anil K. Dabral, learned counsel for the petitioner, would
contend, placing reliance on the supplementary affidavit filed by him, that
sale of meat and chicken continues unabated in the other districts of the State.
This issue falls beyond the scope of the present Writ Petition which is filed
questioning the action of the District Magistrate, Haridwar in prohibiting the
sale of chicken.
7. It is not even the case of the petitioner, in the present Writ
Petition, that sale of meat and chicken should be prohibited in other districts
of the State.
 8. Since the action of the District Magistrate, Haridwar is in
compliance with the order of the Division Bench in Writ Petition (PIL)
No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018, such action cannot be faulted.
9. While dismissing the Writ Petition, we leave it open to the
petitioner, if he so chooses, to question the failure of the State Government
in preventing slaughter of animals in other districts of the State. No costs.
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C. J.)
 27.11.2019 27.11.2019
NISHANT
